issues.description: The problem statement requires calling an external function exit_func with an integer status code, but the provided solution calls exit_func without passing any parameter (no status code is pushed). Additionally, the template does not declare extern exit_func while the solution does. This mismatch between the specification, template, and solution can confuse students about the required call convention and which repository files they must modify.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the template and solution consistently reflect the requirement: add 'extern exit_func' to the template (so students see the external symbol) and modify the call to pass an integer status code (e.g., push 0) before 'call exit_func' in the solution and any example/template code. This makes the requirement explicit and the solution fully compliant with the problem statement.

issues.description: The template uses the non-existent register name 'ecc' (add eax, ecc) while the problem statement instructs to change it to 'ecx' and the solution uses 'ecx' (add eax, ecx). This typo in the template causes a mismatch between the exercise description, the starter code, and the reference solution and will prevent students from mapping the requirement to the implementation and from compiling.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace 'ecc' with the correct register name 'ecx' in helloWorld.asm (change add eax, ecc to add eax, ecx) so the template matches the problem statement and the solution.
